text: Does the KdV soliton (v=1.5 sech^2(x+8)) survive encounter with the Burgers bore (u=1.5*(1-tanh(x/0.5))/2) in the coupled BKdV system on [-15,15] at T=8? Specifically: does v maintain peak >= 0.5 and u stay bounded (|u_max| < 5)?

method: Fourier pseudospectral, 2/3-rule dealiasing, classical RK4 (all terms explicit), no viscosity
bank_use_rationale: BKdV-S1 CLOSED confirms 2/3 dealiasing + RK4 + dt=2e-4 is the working stack; CLOSED central-FD entries rule out FD spatial discretization. BKdV-S6 (OPEN) warns bore IC causes u_max ~2.3x overshoot without viscosity, but since v_max remained 0.58 at T=6 in that experiment — still above our 0.5 target — running no-viscosity baseline is the smallest meaningful first experiment to observe the actual failure mode at T=8.

diagnostics.phenomenon: soliton transmitted through bore: v_max depressed to 0.52 during bore crossing (t=3-4), re-emerged at 0.84 (t=6-7), retained as 0.61 at T=8; bore steepened (u_max 1.5->4.17) but did not blow up

rationale: Both phenomenon targets met: v_peak=0.6076>=0.5 (soliton survived), |u_max|=4.1691<5 (bore bounded). Mass conserved to machine precision. Trajectory shows clear soliton transmission through bore, with depression during passage and partial re-emergence. No NaN. Early stop justified.

F1 meets both phenomenon targets (v_peak=0.608>=0.5, u_max=4.17<5) with all-finite output and machine-precision mass conservation. The bore-soliton interaction is clearly resolved over 9 snapshots. No need to add viscosity or change method.
